name: LAMC2
summary: LAMC2, junctional epidermolysis bullosa type 1 (JEB1), the form found in Belgian and related draft breeds, including the Trait Breton, Trait Comtois and Italian Draft - a recessive lethal. A single cytosine inserted in exon 10 (1368insC) cuts short the gamma-2 chain of laminin-332, the protein that anchors the outer skin to the layer beneath, so the skin and mucous membranes blister and come away. A different gene from LAMA3 (JEB2), so a horse can carry one and be clear of the other.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: LAMC2 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of jeb. The horse is completely normal and there is no way to see it - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way junctional epidermolysis bullosa (lamc2) appears.

phenotypes.name: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (LAMC2)
phenotypes.description: The layer that anchors the outer skin to the body does not hold. The skin and the lining of the mouth blister and come away, and the hoof wall may detach so that the hooves slough. The foal does not survive.
